cards.explanation: The answer is three hundred, friends. Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the officers, wielded his spear against three hundred men and killed them at one time. I get nervous when a batch has three dozen cookies and one is crooked. Three HUNDRED men, one spear, and he just kept going.

The answer is False. The troops fled. The Philistines gathered at Pas-dammim for battle, and at a field full of barley the troops ran from them (1 Chronicles 11:13). When I hear a battle is coming, I'm the first one under the counter. So I can't judge those troops one bit.

The answer is that they stood in the middle of the field and defended it. While the troops fled, Eleazar and David stationed themselves in the middle of the field and defended it. They struck down the Philistines too. Two men in the middle of a field while everybody else leaves, friends. That's a lot of nerve.

The answer is the LORD, friends. Eleazar and David struck down the Philistines, and the text says, "…the LORD brought about a great victory." The two men did the fighting, and the credit for the victory goes to the LORD. That's worth remembering whenever you finish something big.

The answer is Bethlehem, friends. David said, "Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!" The text says the garrison of the Philistines was at Bethlehem at that time. Of all the wells to wish for, he picked one in a town with a Philistine garrison.

The answer is that David pours it out to the LORD. The Three broke through a Philistine camp to bring him water, and he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out to the LORD. I think that tells us how much those men's gift meant to him.

The answer is True, and David says it himself. He says, "How can I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives?" The text adds that because they had brought it at the risk of their lives, David refused to drink it. A water run turned into a risk of lives, and he treated it that way.

The answer is False, friends. Abishai was doubly honored above the Three and became their commander, "…even though he was not included among the Three." He's the boss of a team he isn't officially on. If that happened at my bakery, I'd need a minute to understand the org chart.

The answer is Moab, friends. Benaiah son of Jehoiada, a man of valor from Kabzeel, struck down two champions of Moab. The text calls him a man of many exploits, and this is one of them. On a snowy day he also went down into a pit and killed a lion.

The answer is that he goes down into the pit and kills the lion, and the text says it was a snowy day. Most people see a lion in a pit and stay on the top side, very politely. Benaiah went down. The text calls him a man of valor and a man of many exploits.

The answer is that Benaiah snatches the spear and kills the Egyptian with it. The Egyptian's spear was like a weaver's beam, but Benaiah went against him with a club, snatched the spear from his hand, and killed the Egyptian with his own spear. The text says the Egyptian was a huge man, five cubits tall. I'd say a club against that spear is a bold way to show up.

The answer is True, friends. The text says Benaiah "…was most honored among the Thirty, but he did not become one of the Three." Out of the whole group of Thirty, nobody beat him on honor. He still didn't reach the Three, which is a funny spot to be in.

The answer is guard, friends. Benaiah did not become one of the Three, but the text says David appointed him over his guard. It also says he was most honored among the Thirty. The text puts those two facts side by side.
